records.issue_text: [BUG] Second occurrence of the same wrong-alias cleanup: get("alias") instead of get("idp-alias-20") for the provider created with alias "idp-alias-20". The hideOnLogin IDP created in step 1 is never removed by cleanup, polluting the test realm for later tests in OrganizationCacheTest that assert on realm IDP counts (e.g. getByOrganization assertions).
records.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, the cleanup registered after creating IDPs uses `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` (both in the initial loop creating `idp-alias-0..19` and again after creating `idp-alias-20`). Since `IdentityProvidersResource#get(String alias)` expects the actual alias, passing the literal string "alias" will not target the created provider (e.g., "idp-alias-20"), so the created IDPs are not removed by cleanup and can pollute later tests relying on realm IDP state/counts.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The second cache-population branch calls cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) instead of passing the `loaded` revision read immediately after invalidation, unlike the first branch which uses the loaded revision (startupRevision protocol). The revisioned query is registered under a revision different from the one the delegate read was performed at, so a concurrent invalidation occurring between the read and the addRevisioned is lost — the stale IDP list stays served from cache indefinitely instead of being discarded, showing removed/disabled identity providers on the login page.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Invalidation coverage depends entirely on IDP mutations flowing through create/update/remove of this provider; the diff has no invalidation (and no verification) for organization linkage changes made through OrganizationProvider's own paths (org.identityProviders().remove, or addIdentityProvider on an already-BROKER_PUBLIC idp with no config change), which is exactly the mutation the update-path javadoc says must invalidate. Step 4 of the test only proves invalidation for the BROKER_PUBLIC config change; if OrganizationProvider links/unlinks an IDP without a corresponding identityProviders().update call, the login caches keep the old membership and users see (or miss) IDPs on the org login page until some unrelated invalidation fires.

records.issue_text: [BUG] getForLogin returns organization-aware wrapped models on the cache-miss/invalid path but raw (unwrapped) models on the cache-hit path, breaking the method's contract consistency. Callers that depend on the wrapped OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel behavior (the very behavior the OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean re-check of isEnabled in this diff compensates for) get different objects depending on whether the query was served from cache; the added `idp.isEnabled()` filter in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean line 75/80 is a symptom patch that masks the cache-hit path serving stale/unwrapped state rather than fixing the invariant that both paths return identical models.

records.issue_text: [BUG] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate skips invalidation when an IDP's BROKER_PUBLIC config flag changes but its org link and login-qualifying status stay the same. records.issue_text: [BUG] The new clause in getLoginPredicate excludes org-linked, non-BROKER_PUBLIC IDPs from every fetch mode, including org-specific queries where those IDPs are supposed to be listed. getLoginPredicate is the shared filter the delegate storage providers apply across all FetchMode values; adding `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || BROKER_PUBLIC` means an IDP linked to an organization without the public flag is filtered out even for getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL, thatOrgId) — the org's own login page and member login flow silently lose their non-public broker entries, which per the BROKER_PUBLIC contract are meant to be visible only on the org-specific page (the only place they are ever shown). The integration test only creates org-linked IDPs with BROKER_PUBLIC=true (i >= 10 sets it for all of them), so this regression is invisible to the new test.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup registration calls testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") with the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, and .get returns null for that nonexistent alias, so the `::remove` method reference dereferences null immediately. The very first loop iteration throws NullPointerException inside the test body (the method reference `null::remove` is evaluated on a null Resource at `get("alias")::remove`), failing testCacheIDPForLogin before any caching behavior is exercised and leaving all created IDPs uncleaned for subsequent tests.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The added `idp.isEnabled()` re-filter (justified by the comment 'idp might have been wrapped') shows the caching layer changed what getForLogin returns — raw/cached models instead of organization-aware wrapped models — and the burden of preserving the previous behavior was pushed into one caller. Only OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean was patched; any other existing or future caller of IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin that relied on receiving pre-filtered, organization-wrapped models (e.g., other login templates or extensions) now receives un-wrapped models that may be disabled or lack organization context, and will silently render wrong login options.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cache-miss path in getForLogin wraps results with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, but the cache-hit path (lines 240-248) resolves IDPs via session.identityProviders().getById(id), which returns the plain cached IdentityProviderModel without the organization-aware wrapping. The organization-aware wrapper is what hides an IDP from the login page when its organization is not public or is member-only (the OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean diff's own 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped' comment confirms wrapping can flip enabled state). A user hitting the cached path gets the unwrapped model, so an IDP linked to a non-public organization that was cached under a different organizationId/searchKey context can be rendered on the realm's public login page, disclosing the existence of organization-internal identity providers to unauthenticated users.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Login-cache invalidation is triggered only from the IDP create/update/remove paths in this provider; mutations that change which IDPs are login-visible but are performed through the OrganizationProvider (linking/unlinking an IDP to an organization, or disabling the organization itself) do not pass through these methods, so registerIDPLoginInvalidation is never invoked for them. An admin who unlinks an IDP from an organization (or disables the organization) through the organization management endpoints serves stale cached login lists that still expose the old IDP-to-organization mapping on the public login page until some unrelated IDP write invalidates the cache — a stale-authorization-surface window the diff's own test only avoids because it manually calls the IDP update first.
